evidence.excerpt: Gatik and the Qatar Investment Authority newsrooms, 25 Aug 2026: Gatik announced $200 million in Series D financing co-led by QIA and Koch Disruptive Technologies, with participation from Millennium Management, ARK Invest, Intact Private Capital and others, as demand accelerates for driverless commercial freight across Fortune 50 retail, grocery and CPG supply chains. Announced from Gatik's Santa Clara, California headquarters and carried by Business Wire, Forbes (25 Aug) and PYMNTS.

Gatik's own Series D announcement, 25 Aug 2026: more than $600 million in contracted revenue, 85,000 fully driverless orders completed and 99% on-time delivery. Gatik's network covers the middle mile, moving ambient, refrigerated and frozen goods on high-frequency regional routes between distribution centres and stores for enterprises including Walmart, Kroger and PepsiCo. The company is targeting more than 100 driverless trucks by the end of 2026 and thousands in the years ahead. Corroborated by Forbes, FleetOwner and Sourcing Journal, 25-26 Aug 2026. Deal size in the brief ($1.5-3M a year) is 1440's own ESTIMATE, not a quoted or reported price.

Gatik and Business Wire, May 2024: Isuzu invested US$30 million in Gatik to develop an autonomous-driving logistics business in North America, the two companies jointly designing a new chassis compatible with an autonomous-driving system, targeting a Level 4 commercial-vehicle business and mass production from 2027. Gatik's Level 4 trucks run on NVIDIA compute (Gatik/Isuzu/NVIDIA announcement, Mar 2025); Gatik operates medium-duty Isuzu trucks.

Gatik leadership as listed by the company, The Org and Craft: Gautam Narang, CEO and Co-Founder; Arjun Narang, CTO and Co-Founder; Apeksha Kumavat, Chief Engineer and Co-Founder; Patrick Archambault, Chief Financial Officer; Paul Dilaura, Chief Commercial Officer; Judi Otteson, Chief Legal Officer. No chief marketing officer is listed. No motorsport role appears in any leader's history.

Williams Racing and GlobeNewswire, 13 Nov 2024: Zoox, the autonomous ride-hailing company and independent subsidiary of Amazon, became an Official Regional Partner of Williams Racing in a multi-year agreement — the first time an autonomous-vehicle company had partnered a Formula 1 team. Zoox branding runs on the car at the team's American races. The sponsor table records Zoox as active at Atlassian Williams Racing and Luminar as departed from Mercedes.

Sponsor table: no autonomy, ADAS or autonomous-vehicle partner appears on any 2026 Formula E roster; on the Formula 1 grid Zoox is active at Atlassian Williams Racing and Luminar has departed Mercedes. Lola Yamaha ABT Formula E Team: Lola Cars, Yamaha and ABT Sportsline as brand parents, with Castore (sportswear), OMP (race suits) and Shell (energy/lubricants) as the only major partners — no software, data, AI or technology partner. Andretti Formula E: TWG AI as primary partner and Official Artificial Intelligence Partner. Envision Racing: Sand Technologies (AI). Jaguar TCS Racing: TCS as title, Castrol, Chase in financial services. Mahindra Racing: Tech Mahindra. Porsche Formula E Team: TDK as official technology partner. DS Penske: DS Automobiles and Penske Autosport parents, Mouser Electronics, TTI, Molex, KYOCERA AVX, TotalEnergies. DHL is the logistics partner at championship level in both Formula E and Formula 1; Ceva Logistics sits at Scuderia Ferrari.

brief.deck: Gatik announced a $200M Series D on 25 August, co-led by the Qatar Investment Authority and Koch Disruptive Technologies, on more than $600M of contracted driverless freight. A direct peer already runs on a Formula 1 car; no Formula E team carries an autonomy partner.
brief.team_label: Lola Yamaha ABT Formula E Team
brief.the_case_p1: Gatik announced $200M of Series D financing from Santa Clara on 25 August, co-led by the Qatar Investment Authority and Koch Disruptive Technologies, with Millennium Management, ARK Invest and Intact Private Capital following. The company reports more than $600M of contracted revenue, 85,000 completed fully driverless orders and 99% on-time delivery, moving ambient, refrigerated and frozen goods between distribution centres and stores for Walmart, Kroger and PepsiCo. It is targeting more than 100 driverless trucks by the end of 2026.
brief.the_case_p2: Motorsport has priced this category once already. In November 2024 Zoox, Amazon's robotaxi business, became an Official Regional Partner of Atlassian Williams Racing in Formula 1's first autonomous-vehicle partnership, running on the car at that team's American races. It answers the obvious objection - that a safety-first autonomy company has no business in racing - because a direct peer made the argument first, and won it.
brief.why_now_callout: <font name='Poppins-Bold' size='9'>WHY NOW</font>  The Series D landed on 25 August and category budgets are written in the quarter after a raise. brief.why_team_para: The sponsor table records no autonomy, software or data partner anywhere on the Formula E grid, and Lola Yamaha ABT carries the thinnest technology roster on it: Castore, OMP and Shell beside the Lola Cars, Yamaha and ABT Sportsline parents. An autonomous-technology designation would be a first there, not a slot. Yamaha's Japanese engineering base sits alongside Gatik's Isuzu alliance rather than against it, and Season 13 finishes in Tokyo.

Estimated $1.5-3M a year. Scope: sidepod and halo placement, naming rights on the team's data and simulation programme, US and Tokyo hospitality, joint engineering content.
brief.decision_maker_bio: Narang co-founded Gatik with Arjun Narang and Apeksha Kumavat and fronts every raise; a first sports partnership is his call. Path: Paul Dilaura, chief commercial officer, who owns commercial spend, and Patrick Archambault, chief financial officer. No chief marketing officer is listed.
brief.opening_angle_intro: Lead with Zoox, not with the trucks.
brief.opening_angle_quote: “Gautam, Zoox took Formula 1's first autonomous-vehicle seat at Williams in 2024. No Formula E team has sold one yet and it costs a fraction of that. 25 minutes to look at the Lola Yamaha ABT numbers?”
score_cells: Round announced 25 Aug; Season 13 rosters close this autumn.
$200M Series D on $600M+ of contracted revenue; QIA and Koch behind it.
Zoox proves the category buys racing; the buyer is still a supply-chain VP.
No deadline; the 2027 Isuzu launch is the only clock.
MODE B: a designation and a stage, not a team workstream.
risks: A driverless-freight company's proposition is that its trucks are unexciting and safe. Racing says the opposite, and no autonomy peer but Zoox has bought motorsport.
Zoox answered it in Formula 1. Buy the engineering story - perception, simulation, validation - and activate at the rounds where the customers already are.
The $200M was raised to put 100+ driverless trucks on the road by the end of 2026 and reach mass production with Isuzu in 2027, not to buy brand.
Formula E prices the designation at a fraction of Formula 1, and a three-year term spreads it across the production ramp.
brief.bottom_line: A $200M Series D on 25 August, more than $600M of contracted revenue and a direct peer already running on a Formula 1 car put Gatik at the moment an autonomy brand decides whether to become visible. Formula E has never sold an autonomy seat, and the Lola Yamaha ABT roster carries no technology partner at all.

why_now.label: The trigger
why_now.text: Gatik announced $200M of Series D financing on 25 August 2026 from its Santa Clara headquarters, co-led by the Qatar Investment Authority and Koch Disruptive Technologies, with Millennium Management, ARK Invest and Intact Private Capital participating. Both Gatik's and QIA's own newsrooms carry it, so the round is company-confirmed rather than reported.

why_now.label: The business under the round
why_now.text: Gatik states more than $600M of contracted revenue, 85,000 completed fully driverless orders and 99% on-time delivery. Its network is the middle mile: ambient, refrigerated and frozen goods on high-frequency regional routes between distribution centres and stores for Walmart, Kroger and PepsiCo. These are the company's own figures from its release, not audited accounts.

why_now.label: The production clock
why_now.text: Isuzu put $30M into Gatik in 2024 and the two are jointly developing a chassis built for a Level 4 system, running on NVIDIA compute, targeting mass production from 2027. Gatik is aiming for more than 100 driverless trucks by the end of 2026 and thousands beyond that. A brand programme agreed now runs into that ramp rather than trailing it.

why_now.label: The calendar
why_now.text: Formula E teams close Season 13 rosters through the autumn. The season opens at the Jeddah E-Prix on 18 December 2026 and runs 21 races across 13 cities, with the Austin E-Prix on 6 February 2027, the Miami E-Prix two weeks later and the Tokyo E-Prix closing on 24-25 July 2027.

why_team.label: An empty category, and a proven one
why_team.text: The sponsor table shows no autonomy, ADAS or autonomous-vehicle partner on any 2026 Formula E roster. In Formula 1 the same category is already sold: Zoox has been an Official Regional Partner of Atlassian Williams Racing since November 2024, in what both parties called Formula 1's first autonomous-vehicle partnership. The archetype is proven and the Formula E version of it is unsold.

why_team.label: The thinnest technology roster on the grid
why_team.text: Lola Yamaha ABT's major partners are Castore, OMP and Shell - sportswear, race suits and lubricants - beside the Lola Cars, Yamaha and ABT Sportsline parents. There is no software, data, AI or technology partner. That means an autonomous-technology designation is available as a first rather than as an addition, and the partner sits beside a constructor brand rather than behind a car marque.

why_team.label: No manufacturer conflict
why_team.text: Gatik's chassis partner and investor is Isuzu, which is co-developing the Level 4 truck for 2027. That rules out the Formula E entries fronted by commercial-vehicle makers - Nissan, Mahindra, Citroen and Cupra Kiro through the Volkswagen Group - because Isuzu could reasonably object to its autonomy partner branding a rival manufacturer's works team. Lola is a constructor, ABT is an operator and Yamaha builds engines and components, so none of them competes with Isuzu.

why_team.label: Why Formula E and not Formula 1
why_team.text: Three reasons. The Formula 1 autonomy lane is held by a direct peer at Williams, so entering Formula 1 means either following Zoox or partnering a team that has already been passed over for it. Formula E races on city streets, which is where public and regulatory acceptance of driverless vehicles is actually contested. And a Formula E designation is affordable for a company whose $200M round is earmarked for fleet and safety validation, which a Formula 1 team-major position is not.

value.label: Mode B, stated honestly
value.text: There is no operational workstream here and the brief does not pretend otherwise. No Formula E team will deploy an autonomous middle-mile freight stack, and any claim that it would is a claim 1440 will not make. What follows is what the partnership actually delivers on both sides.

value.label: What the team gets
value.text: Its first technology partner and a designation it has never sold, at a moment when its commercial roster is three consumer-goods brands. A co-produced engineering content strand pairing Lola's constructor heritage and Yamaha's powertrain work with a driverless-freight story that reads as engineering rather than advertising. And a partner whose growth is contracted rather than speculative.

value.label: What Gatik gets
value.text: A category designation nobody else in autonomous freight holds. Hospitality at the Austin, Miami and Tokyo rounds for the retail and CPG buyers it sells to - Walmart, Kroger and PepsiCo all operate at scale in those markets - and for QIA, Koch, ARK and Millennium on the investor side. A recruiting channel into perception, controls and simulation engineering, where motorsport and autonomy hire from the same pool.

value.label: The commercial shape
value.text: Official Autonomous Technology Partner, three years across Seasons 13 to 15 so the term covers the Isuzu mass-production launch in 2027. Estimated at $1.5-3M a year - an estimate, not a quoted price. Scope: sidepod and halo placement, naming rights on the team's data and simulation programme, hospitality at the US and Tokyo rounds, and joint engineering content.

Ceva Logistics sits on the roster and DHL is the championship logistics partner in both series; the freight adjacency is crowded.

# Gatik → Lola Yamaha ABT Formula E Team — verification log (N° 234, 25 Aug 2026)

An n8n-engine row (4 Sep 2026, score 77, WARM, person Gautam Narang) rebuilt as a full case at no
model-API cost. Nothing n8n recorded was carried over; the trigger, the score, the person and the
team were all re-derived from live search.

**Sandbox limitation, stated plainly:** direct fetches of gatik.ai, qia.qa, williamsf1.com,
forbes.com, fleetowner.com and motorsport.com were blocked by the egress proxy. Every claim below
was checked against the search summary of the primary page named as the evidence URL. Treat each
VERIFIED line as REPORTED until a person opens the link. Confidence is MEDIUM and the footer reads
VERIFY BEFORE CIRCULATION.

## The trigger

**$200M Series D, announced 25 August 2026**, co-led by the **Qatar Investment Authority** and
**Koch Disruptive Technologies**, with Millennium Management, ARK Invest and Intact Private Capital
participating. It carries on **both** Gatik's own newsroom and QIA's own newsroom, so it is
company-confirmed rather than press-reported — the strongest class of trigger the engine takes.
It is 12 days before today, well inside the 90-day window, so the signal sits on 25 Aug 2026 rather
than on the 4 Sep row date n8n recorded.

## The screen-out that was considered and rejected, twice

This case was drafted as a **screen-out** and then re-opened, and the reasoning is worth recording.

1. **First pass — below threshold.** Autonomous freight has no operational workstream at a race
   team; the buyer is a Fortune 50 supply-chain executive who is not in the grandstand; the $200M is
   earmarked for fleet and safety validation; and a driverless-trucking brand arguably cannot afford
   to be associated with speed. On those pillars the honest score landed at 67 — below 70, so no case.
2. **What changed it.** A clash-check of the sponsor table turned up **Zoox, active at Atlassian
   Williams Racing**, and Luminar (lidar) as a departed Mercedes partner. An autonomous-vehicle
   company has therefore already bought a Formula 1 seat, in a multi-year deal that both parties
   billed as the sport's first AV partnership. That is a verified category precedent, and it answers
   the off-brand objection empirically rather than by assertion. Brand fit moves from 12 to 14 and
   the signal clears at **71** — a genuine HOT, not an inflated one.

The first-pass objections are not buried: the off-brand risk is the first risk row, the earmarked
capital is the second, and the Mode B disclosure is the first paragraph of the value section on the
app page.

## The team choice, and a false lead that was killed

**DS Penske was the first pick and it was wrong.** The thesis was that Penske Truck Leasing — a
440,000-vehicle North American fleet business — would give Gatik a commercial path through the
team's owner. A live check killed it: the Formula E entry is **Jay Penske's** Penske Autosport
(formerly Dragon Racing), not Roger Penske's Penske Corporation, and DS Automobiles is reported to
be leaving the championship after the London finale. Neither half of the thesis survived, and DS
Penske is ruled out on the record rather than quietly dropped.

**The manufacturer clash-check drove the final choice.** Isuzu is a $30M investor co-developing
Gatik's 2027 truck, so Formula E entries fronted by commercial-vehicle manufacturers are out on
conflict: Nissan, Mahindra, Citroen and Cupra Kiro (Volkswagen Group). Andretti and Envision are out
on an occupied AI lane, Jaguar on TCS, Porsche on TDK. Lola Yamaha ABT is what survives — and it
survives positively, not by elimination: it has no software, data or technology partner at all, its
parents are a constructor, an operator and an engine maker rather than a car marque, and Season 13
finishes at Yamaha's home round in Tokyo.

## Honest score — what holds it back (71, not the 77 n8n recorded)

- **Ops fit 12/20.** Mode B. No team deploys an autonomous-freight stack, and the brief says so in
  the first line of the value section. That single pillar is what keeps this out of the 80s.
- **Urgency 12/20.** There is no deadline. The Isuzu mass-production launch in 2027 is a ramp, not
  a cliff, and the decision can slip two quarters at no cost.
- **Brand fit 14/20.** Zoox proves the category will buy racing, but Gatik's purchase decision sits
  with a supply-chain executive at Walmart or PepsiCo, not with a Formula E viewer.
- **Capacity 16/20.** $200M is real money, but it is raised against a fleet target, and a Series D
  company is a smaller cheque than the mature public names this desk usually scores in the 80s.

## Leadership ties

`leadership_ties`: **none found**. Gautam Narang, Arjun Narang, Apeksha Kumavat, Patrick
Archambault, Paul Dilaura and Judi Otteson show no Formula 1 or Formula E role in any listing
checked, and no prior sponsorship deal structured by any of them was found.

## Not claimed

- **No revenue figure is presented as audited.** "$600M of contracted revenue" is the company's own
  number from its own release and is attributed that way in the copy.
- **No valuation** is stated: none was disclosed with the Series D and none is inferred.
- **No total-funding figure** is used: the reported totals varied across secondary sources.
- **Deal size ($1.5-3M a year) is an ESTIMATE** and is labelled as such on the app page.
- **DHL holds logistics at championship level in both series** and Ceva Logistics sits at Ferrari.
  Gatik is autonomous-driving software rather than a freight forwarder, so this is treated as an
  adjacency and named in the rule-outs, not as a hard clash.
